THE STAR AT THE CENTRE

Meet our Sun.

Our nearest star powers life on Earth.
Get to know the heart of our solar system.

☉ SOL
G2 V · YELLOW DWARF STAR

A star with a big role.

The Sun is a glowing ball of plasma made mostly of hydrogen and helium. Its gravity keeps the planets in orbit, while its light and heat help sustain life on Earth.

Explore the Sun at NASA ↗

Artistic illustration · Not to scale

All values are approximate. Rotation varies with latitude because the Sun is not solid. Sources: NASA Sun facts, NASA Sun fact sheet, and ESA.

01 / ITS POWER SOURCE

Fusion, not fire.

Deep in the core, hydrogen nuclei join to form helium. This nuclear fusion releases the energy that makes the Sun shine.

02 / A SOLAR HEAVYWEIGHT

Almost all the mass.

The Sun holds about 99.8% of the solar system’s mass. Its powerful gravity shapes the paths of planets, asteroids, and comets.

03 / ALWAYS CHANGING

Spots, flares, and solar wind.

Sunspots are cooler patches on the visible surface. Magnetic activity can trigger solar flares, and charged particles flow outward as the solar wind.

01

Why only eight planets?

Pluto is a dwarf planet. It shares its orbital neighbourhood with other objects, unlike the eight major planets.

02

What about the Sun?

The Sun is a star at the centre of our solar system. Its gravity keeps the planets travelling around it.
